articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Current Mode Analogue Circuits' (Digest No.25)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Current Mode Analogue Circuits
IEE Colloquium on Current Mode Analogue Circuits
abstract: Conventional resistive feedback differential amplifiers, including the standard three op-amp instrumentation amplifier, require precisely matched resistors to achieve high CMRR. The circuit described in this paper uses op-amp supply-current sensing techniques to obtain high CMRR performance over a wider bandwidth than conventional designs. A feature of this design is its simplicity and that precisely matched resistors are not required.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Continuous-time and switched capacitor monolithic filters based on current and charge simulation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Current Mode Analogue Circuits
abstract: An important area of application of analogue circuits is for the realisation of high precision integrated circuit filters. Although the adoption of current processing may eventually lead to very high frequency filters, at this stage the authors examine benefits of current processing from the points of view of minimising sensitivity of response to component parameter variations and also maximising signal handling capability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and application of GaAs MESFET current mirror circuits
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Current Mode Analogue Circuits
abstract: It is well known that the techniques and approaches of circuit design are heavily influenced by the fabrication technology involved. High speed Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) technology is generally regarded as a challenge for circuit designers, principally on account of the lack of a P-channel device, low device gain and, in general, limitation to depletion mode devices. In this paper, the authors show that, unlike bipolar technology, GaAs technology using metal semiconductor FETs (MESFETs) permits the design of a simple fast circuit for the negative current mirror, which has a beneficial effect across a wide range of circuit applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of artificial neural networks using current mode analogue circuit techniques
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Current Mode Analogue Circuits
abstract: The logistic function is a close approximation to the biological neuron's dendritic input (graded response) versus the output activation (number of action potentials/second). It also has some useful mathematical characteristics and the resulting output is a unipolar signal. An artificial neural network is constructed by cascading these simple neurons in structures consisting of one or more layers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Current Mode Analogue Circuits
abstract: Second generation current conveyors have, since their formulation by Sedra and Smith in 1970, proved to be functionally flexible and versatile, rapidly gaining acceptance as both theoretical and practical building blocks in a wide range of applications from immittance convertors through to active filter synthesis. That current conveyors may be used as voltage amplifiers is also well known, but has in the past only rarely been of practical significance due to the relatively poor performance of conveyor realisations compared to standard voltage operational amplifiers (VOA). However, with the introduction by Wilson in 1984 of a new conveyor implementation their performance can now challenge, and often exceed, standard VOAs in many applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A sensitive integrated CMOS charge comparator
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Current Mode Analogue Circuits
abstract: The motivation behind this research was to design and fabricate an integrated circuit which is a position-sensitive detector for low energy (typically <or=100 eV) charged particles. The actual device comprises a linear array of electron-sensing electrodes coupled to detection and read-out circuitry in the form of amplifiers and counters all integrated onto a single CMOS IC. The chip is intended to replace existing position-sensitive detection systems in electron spectrometers. The chip is mounted in a vacuum and needs to be capable of detecting incident charge-pulses that consist of, typically, 10/sup 5/ to 10/sup 6/ electrons.<<ETX>>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Current Mode Analogue Circuits
abstract: Many analogue systems-BJT and MOS-including those employing current mode signal processing techniques, involve current mirrors. In many cases, it is desirable that the Current Transfer Ratio should be accurately defined. Methods of trimming to achieve accuracy are not considered in this paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analogue sampled-data signal processing for VLSI using switched currents
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Current Mode Analogue Circuits
abstract: Process parameters, particularly threshold voltage, will be chosen to optimise digital performance, and the performance of the op amps and analogue switches required to operate in the voltage domain will suffer. So, future analogue circuits for VLSI applications face both economic and technical difficulties, and this paper offers a solution using a new analogue sampled-data technique, called switched currents, requiring only a baseline digital process and avoiding many of the anticipated low voltage problems by operating in the current domain.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
